title: SSE: resilient fragment recovery with sequence checks + explicit function-call boundaries
author: Ava Patel
body: Summary: Fixes several classes of SSE streaming corruption that manifested as partial/invalid JSON payloads at the client, out-of-order tool/function call sentinel emission, and duplicate or missing event delimiters during aggressive chunk coalescing. The core approach is threefold: (1) carry an explicit per-event sequence marker inside the SSE event metadata so clients can detect and reorder or drop stale fragments; (2) include a lightweight checksum (CRC8) over the event payload to detect silent truncation/misboundaries; (3) introduce deterministic function-call boundary markers (␞ token + explicit header) that are impossible to be generated by model text and are recognized by the OpenAI-compat layer and SDKs as strong sentinels for structured output and tool calling. This makes streaming compatible with clients that rely on strict JSON framing and reduces heuristics needed to reconstruct partial JSON objects.
commits: c1e9f6d: introduce event seq field and crc8 to sse framing
b3a4d98: implement decoder rollback + resequencing logic in sse_decoder.py
9f2a7b1: add function-call sentinel token generation and parser hooks
e0c5d77: E2E test: sse_replay_e2e.test.js covers out-of-order and truncated fragments
d4b7fa2: update docs/compat/streaming.md and migration notes
a7f3d2b: squash/fixup: address review comments and add more test permutations
review_comments: Diego Martinez (requested changes): Please explain why CRC8 is sufficient vs CRC16 for adversarial networks. Also add a flag to opt-out for legacy clients.
Ava Patel (author reply): Chose CRC8 for minimal overhead and single-byte sentinel; added opt-out via compatibility_mode flag and documented tradeoffs in the streaming.md section.
Sophie Chen (comment): Decoder rollback looks good but add a couple negative tests where sequence numbers wrap and where multiple in-flight fragments reference same seq.
testing_notes: Added deterministic fuzz table-driven tests for: trimmed chunk midpoint, duplicate delimiter sequences, coalesced multiple events in single chunk, out-of-order arrival (seq swap), truncated event with checksum mismatch. E2E harness reproduces a historical SUP-4021 incident and asserts client-level JSON validity across restarts.
backwards_compatibility: This change is opt-in for server clients by default on new deployments. A compatibility_mode flag in the OpenAI-compat config disables seq+crc headers to preserve legacy behavior. SDKs (python/ts) are updated to recognize sentinels but fall back when headers absent.
migration_instructions: Operators: rollout server-side config 'enable_sse_seq_crc' behind a feature flag; perform canary in a low-traffic region. Client SDKs detect sentinel tokens and will upgrade parsing logic without breaking older servers.
release_notes: Fix: Improved SSE stream resilience by adding sequence numbers and checksums to detect and recover from partial JSON frames; added explicit function-call boundary sentinels to guarantee structured output integrity across chunk boundaries. Backwards-compatible via config flag.
security_considerations: Checksum and seq metadata are non-sensitive. Added bounds checks in decoder to avoid excessive memory retention on malformed streams. No crypto keys introduced.
notes_for_release: Include migration note in the next SDK changelog; highlight in developer newsletter the reduced incidence of client-side JSON parse errors. Recommend enabling the feature for Dedicated customers after a 48h canary.
acknowledgements: Thanks to the SRE on-call (Marcus Lee) for reproducing the SUP-4021 replay, and to QA (Sophie) for creating the e2e harness permutations.
